prs.title: perf(nuxt): memoise lazy route component imports on the server
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description another one from doing some profiling of nuxt render times. because we create a new router for every request on the server, vue-router's cache of resolved lazy route components never gets reused, and every request pays the overhead of a dynamic import. this PR wraps lazy page components in the generated `#build/routes` with a small `memoizeRouteComponent` helper on the server in production builds, so every router reuses the same promise. | app | main | branch | delta | | - | - | - | - | | single-SFC page | 352µs | 336µs | -4.5% | the savings grow by the number of components imported, so nested pages should show more improvement.

prs.title: fix(vite): use a single type checker
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue resolves #36738 ### 📚 Description since the environment api refactor (#33445) we've been creating a separate `vite-plugin-checker` instance for the `client` and `ssr` environments. the ssr worker was also never terminated, so with `typescript.typeCheck: true` each soft reload leaked one checker worker along with its program and file watchers. that part is now fixed upstream in https://github.com/fi3ework/vite-plugin-checker/pull/833. this PR registers a single checker applied to the client environment, which is what we did before the refactor.

prs.title: fix(vite): pass dev listener to nitro for websocket upgrades
prs.author: benjamincanac
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Needs https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4647

### 📚 Description

With Nitro mounted as a Vite environment, WebSockets don't work in `nuxt dev`. Vite runs in middleware mode, so Nitro has no `httpServer` to listen for upgrades on, and the `nuxt.server` we expose has no `upgrade` for the CLI to forward to, unlike the legacy `createDevServer(nitro)`.

Today an app with `nitro.features.websocket` can't even boot, because Nitro calls `server.httpServer.on("upgrade")` on `null`. That part is nitrojs/nitro#4647. With it fixed the dev server starts, but every upgrade is dropped.

This adds `upgrade` to `nuxt.server` and hands the request to the Nitro environment's dev server, the same call Nitro makes from its own listener outside middleware mode.

`nuxt.server` is assigned once early with only `upgrade`, because the CLI checks `"upgrade" in nuxt.server` right after `ready()`, before `vite:serverCreated` has run. I'm not sure that's the shape you want. The alternative is for the CLI to look `upgrade` up when a request comes in, happy to move it there instead.

Tested by applying both changes to the installed `5.0.0-29833065` and Nitro `3.0.260903-beta` in an app running a WebSocket game loop: `nuxt dev` boots and the socket protocol tests connect and run.
